chunks: I asked him about the hunted prey that the arrow strikes sideways and does not strike it with the iron (arrowhead), and he had named (said Bismillah) when he shot. He said: He may eat it when he struck it and he saw it (fall).

And about the prey hunted by the blunt weapon (mi'rad), he said: If he does not have an arrow other than it, and he had named (said Bismillah) when he threw, then let him eat from it; but if he had an arrow other than it, then no.

key_terms.المعراض: Mi'rad — a blunt headless arrow or stick that kills by its weight/impact rather than by cutting; its use in hunting is a matter of jurisprudential controversy
key_terms.بحديدة: With the iron (arrowhead) — referring to the conventional piercing point of an arrow
key_terms.سمّى: Pronounced the tasmiyyah (Bismillah) — a required condition for the permissibility of hunted game

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat prey struck sideways by an arrow or killed by a blunt weapon (mi'rad) in Islam?
ai.summary: Al-Halabi narrates a ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) on two related hunting scenarios. For prey struck by an arrow sideways (not by the arrowhead), it is permissible to eat if the hunter said Bismillah and witnessed the animal fall. For prey killed by a mi'rad (a headless or blunt wooden arrow), eating is only permitted if the hunter had no other conventional arrows available and said Bismillah — because the mi'rad kills by its weight rather than by cutting, and the availability of a proper arrow makes its use the obligatory method. This hadith reflects classical Shia jurisprudence distinguishing lawful slaughter methods.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Al Magra, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the hunted prey hit by the arrow sideways, and it was not hit by the iron (arrowhead), and he had Named (Bismillah) when he shot it Heasws said: ‘He can eat it when he hit it, and he saw it’.

And about a prey hunted by the blunt weapon, so heasws said: ‘If there does not happen to be an arrow apart from it, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he threw, so let him eat from it; and if there was an arrow apart from it, so, no’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu al-Mighra’ from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a prey which is hit by an arrow widthwise and no iron part has hit it. He had mentioned the name of Allah when shooting. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can use it for food if it hits and he sees it hitting.’

I asked him (the Imam) about hunting with flareless arrows. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has no other arrow and he has mentioned the name of Allah when shooting, he can use it for food; but if he had other arrows then he cannot use it for food.’”
